title: Evaluating RAG and Agent Quality
description: Measure retrieval quality, answer relevance, and agent success rates so you can improve AI backends with data, not guesses.

blocks.text: Production AI backends need evaluation pipelines, not ad hoc testing. Evaluation answers questions such as: Does retrieval return the right chunks? Does the answer stay grounded? Did the agent complete the requested task without side effects?

blocks.title: Common metrics for RAG and agents
items: **Context recall** — does the retrieved context contain the information needed to answer correctly?
**Answer relevance** — does the final answer address the user's question?
**Faithfulness** — is the answer supported by the retrieved context rather than hallucinated?
**Task success rate** — for agents, did the requested task complete successfully?
**Latency and cost** — how long did the pipeline take and how much did it cost?

blocks.title: Conceptual evaluation record
blocks.content: A simple schema to capture evaluation results in C#.
blocks.code:
public sealed record RagEvaluationResult(
    string TestCaseId,
    IReadOnlyList<string> ExpectedSources,
    IReadOnlyList<string> RetrievedChunkIds,
    bool HasAnswer,
    bool IsFaithful,
    bool IsRelevant,
    TimeSpan Latency,
    decimal CostUsd);

blocks.title: Automate evaluations
blocks.text: Run evaluation suites on every change to chunking, retrieval, prompts, or tools. Manual testing cannot keep up with iterative AI development.

items.text: I can define a test case for RAG evaluation
items.hint: Question, expected source chunks, and an ideal answer

items.text: I know the difference between recall and faithfulness
items.hint: Recall asks whether context was retrieved; faithfulness asks whether the answer matches that context

items.text: I can instrument agent loops for success measurement
items.hint: Record task completion, turn count, tool failures, and final answer quality

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Evaluation turns AI backend development into a measurable engineering discipline.
Track retrieval, faithfulness, relevance, cost, and latency.
Automate evaluations and review regressions before deployment.
blocks.takeaway: If you cannot measure it, you cannot improve it. Build evaluation pipelines early, even when they are simple.
